thm:generalMonicCount.title: All monic cubics
thm:generalMonicCount.proof: Reduce each trace class to trace zero or one. Substitute the asymptotic formulas for $A_0$ and $A_1$, approximate their main-term sums by integrals, and then sum the errors. The two real integrals give the displayed polynomial $P$.

thm:asymptoticPolynomialCount.title: Trace-one cubics
thm:asymptoticPolynomialCount.proof: Estimate $\sum_{n\leq X}d_n$ by truncated Perron's formula and contour shifting. Subtract the split contribution and set $X=1+3H^2$. The paper uses Alberts's theorem for the coefficient estimate; Lean retains the direct proof.

thm:exactFormula.title: An exact count
thm:exactFormula.proof: For $n=1-3a$, the torus points are counted by $d_n$. The split points are the free cyclic orbits of $E_{\sqrt n}(\ZZ)$, and each irreducible polynomial contributes two points. Thus the answer is $d_n/2-\#E_{\sqrt n}(\ZZ)/6$.

thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula.title: The one-variable height zeta function
thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula.proof: Restrict the multivariate formula to the height under consideration and identify its Euler factors with those of $\xi$. The correction product is holomorphic in the required half-plane; the Laurent expansion gives the unique double pole.

cor:integralPointCount.title: Integral points
cor:integralPointCount.proof: The coefficient sum counts the integral points with the prescribed height. Insert its asymptotic formula and the Laurent coefficients of $Z_0$.

thm:modularInterpretation.title: Rational points of the moduli space
thm:modularInterpretation.proof: Construct the algebra and normal element from a rational quotient point, and recover the quotient point from the conjugates of the normal element. These constructions are inverse on isomorphism classes. This node states the rational-point part of the paper's theorem.

prop:basicfacts.title: The local logarithm
prop:basicfacts.proof: Express torus points by characters over the splitting field. Applying the normalized valuation gives the finite-place image lattice and compact kernel. The logarithmic absolute value gives the analogous statement at infinity.

lemma:heightformula.title: Weight vectors
lemma:heightformula.proof: Compute the invariant cubic forms, divide by $e_1^3$, and diagonalize the torus action. The four displayed forms and their characters give the required basis of sections.

lemma:affineIntegrality.title: Integral points in the affine chart
lemma:affineIntegrality.proof: Compute the cyclic invariants in the affine chart. The invariant relation makes $\delta$ integral over $\ZZ[e_2,e_3]$, so integral values of $e_2,e_3$ force the rational value of $\delta$ to be integral.

prop:canonicalHeight.title: Integral coefficients and toric height
prop:canonicalHeight.proof: Apply the invariant-ring criterion to the characteristic polynomial. Evaluate the local height factors; their product reduces to $\sqrt{1-3a}$.

lemma:rootVsToric.title: Comparing heights
lemma:rootVsToric.proof: The three roots are real. The resulting coefficient inequalities give $a\leq0$ and $|b|^{2/3}\leq-a$. Substitute this into the root-height definition and use the toric-height formula.

prop:cyclotomicParametrization.title: The Eisenstein parametrization
prop:cyclotomicParametrization.proof: Identify the character lattices, then evaluate the invariant functions in $u+v\zeta$. The norm and trace determine the cubic coefficients. Solving the displayed quadratic gives the fibers, including the repeated-root case, and the coefficient formulas give the integral conditions.

thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula2.title: The multivariate height zeta function
thm:heightZetaFunctionFormula2.proof: Compute the local Fourier transforms, apply Poisson summation, and evaluate the resulting real integral by residues. Shift the height parameters to obtain the full convergence region, then identify the continued Euler product.

prop:localIntegrality.title: The local integral condition
prop:localIntegrality.proof: Away from $3$, evaluate the invariant functions in local coordinates to obtain the cone condition. At $3$, the same computation gives the subgroup $1+3O_{E,w}$. Its stabilizer determines the global compact level.

prop:heightFourierTransform.title: Local Fourier transforms
prop:heightFourierTransform.proof: At infinity and at finite places other than $3$, ramified characters vanish after integration over the maximal compact subgroup. For unramified characters, integrate the archimedean support function on its two cones and sum the finite valuation lattices. At $3$, integrate over the congruence subgroup of index six.

prop:Lmap.title: The adelic logarithm
prop:Lmap.proof: The product formula makes the logarithm descend to the adelic quotient. Principalize the finite valuations to identify its kernel with the compact quotient; the infinite component supplies surjectivity.

lemma:KprimeGroup.title: The quotient by the integral level
lemma:KprimeGroup.proof: The six Eisenstein units represent the residue classes at the ramified place. They identify the quotient by the integral level with the logarithm line. Tracking the normalized Haar measure gives $du/6$.

lemma:finiteFourierProduct.title: The finite Fourier product
lemma:finiteFourierProduct.proof: Sum the local valuation series separately at split and inert primes and include the factor $1/6$ at $3$. A convergent positive Euler product bounds the absolute values and proves locally uniform convergence.

lemma:heightZetaConvergence.title: Convergence before Poisson summation
lemma:heightZetaConvergence.proof: The positive local factors give spatial integrability. The finite Euler-product bound and quadratic decay of the archimedean factor give integrability on the annihilator of $T(\QQ)$.

lemma:poissonIntegral.title: Applying Poisson summation
lemma:poissonIntegral.proof: Apply the general Poisson formula with the normalized quotient measure. Identify the characters trivial on the integral level with the real logarithm coordinate; the dual measure contributes the factor six.

lemma:simplifiedZ(s).title: Dedekind zeta factorization
lemma:simplifiedZ(s).proof: Compare the Euler factors with $\xi(z)^2$ and the correction product $R(z)$. The factorization and convergence of the correction product give the continuation.

prop:leadingTerms.title: Laurent coefficients
prop:leadingTerms.proof: Expand the Dedekind zeta factor at $1$ and logarithmically differentiate the convergent correction product. Simplifying the prime factors yields $\alpha$, $\beta$, and the Euler--Kronecker constant $\mu$.

lemma:normalityCriterion.title: Normality
lemma:normalityCriterion.proof: The Gram determinant of the trace pairing on the conjugates of $x$ is the square of the group determinant. Use its factorization $\Delta=e_1(e_1^2-3e_2)$ and nondegeneracy of the trace form.

lemma:reducibles.title: Removing split polynomials
lemma:reducibles.proof: Use the multiplicities of the characteristic-polynomial map. Count the split points by cyclic orbits of integer triples and compare the corresponding ellipse lattice count with its area.

lemma:xiMeanValue.title: A uniform mean-square estimate
lemma:xiMeanValue.proof: Apply the residue theorem to an exponentially decaying kernel. A reflected kernel keeps the estimate uniform as $\sigma$ approaches $1/2$. Integrate over the height interval and apply the critical-line mean-square bound. The paper instead uses Titchmarsh, \cite[\S7.8, (7.8.3)]{titchmarsh1986}.

eqn:xiMeanBound.title: The strip bound
eqn:xiMeanBound.proof: This is the bound proved in Lemma~\ref{lemma:xiMeanValue}, with the same uniformity in $\sigma$.

eqn:dSummatoryForGeneralTrace.title: The coefficient sum
eqn:dSummatoryForGeneralTrace.proof: Apply truncated Perron at a half-integer, move the contour across the double pole at $1$, and estimate the new contour using the strip mean-square bound. The residue supplies the main term. This is the direct argument retained in Lean in place of \cite[Theorem~1.1]{alberts2025}.

lemma:generalHeightReduction.title: Reducing the trace
lemma:generalHeightReduction.proof: Integer translation, followed by reflection in the third residue class, gives the stated bijections and preserves $n$. The real-root coefficient inequalities reduce the height condition to the two displayed bounds.

lemma:traceZeroCoefficients.title: Trace-zero coefficients
lemma:traceZeroCoefficients.proof: Factor in the Eisenstein integers and separate the valuation at $1-\zeta$. Count the allowed unit multiples. The vanishing-discriminant cases contribute the extra term when $N=3u^2$.

prop:traceZeroAsymptotic.title: The trace-zero count
prop:traceZeroAsymptotic.proof: Sum the coefficient formula over the powers of $3$, apply the asymptotic for the $d_M$, and remove the reducible cubics. The geometric series in the powers of $3$ gives the stated constants.

prop:surfaceIntegralCubic.title: The invariant cubic model
prop:surfaceIntegralCubic.proof: Compute the cyclic invariant ring and its third Veronese. The resulting cubic relation gives the embedding. Adjunction gives the anticanonical class, and the hyperplane intersection has degree three.

prop:surfaceRationalForm.title: The standard rational form
prop:surfaceRationalForm.proof: Apply the explicit change of coordinates over $\ZZ[1/6]$. Split the norm over $E$, and compute the singular points and their local equations. The toric lattice gives the Picard rank.

prop:surfaceResolvedBoundary.title: The resolution and boundary
prop:surfaceResolvedBoundary.proof: Subdivide the three singular cones to obtain the minimal smooth fan. Compute the exceptional chain, divisor classes, and intersections in that fan. The intersection numbers establish the assertions about $L$.

prop:santensConstant.title: The Santens constant
prop:santensConstant.proof: Use the pullback of the affine coordinate ring to express the integral condition. Verify the fan, divisor, and positivity hypotheses, then evaluate the dual-cone volume and the normalized local integrals. Their product is $2\alpha/9$.

rem:idealParametrization.title: The alternative ideal count
rem:idealParametrization.proof: The Eisenstein parametrization identifies integral torus points with ideals of cube norm prime to $3$. Apply the cube-ideal summatory estimate, remove the Euler factor at $3$, and compare the constants and heights.

rem:heightCoefficients.title: The coefficients
rem:heightCoefficients.proof: Expand the split, inert, and ramified Euler factors and multiply the prime-power coefficients.

rem:localNonintegrability.title: Why the parameters are kept separate
rem:localNonintegrability.proof: Along a boundary ray where a height exponent vanishes, the local valuation series has terms of constant absolute value. It therefore fails to converge.

example:twoRationalPointsSamePoly.proof: The Galois group of a cyclic cubic field is abelian. An isomorphism to the inverse-action twist would therefore force a generator to equal its inverse, a contradiction. The cocycles describe the two rational points.

example:splitAlgebra.proof: Every algebra automorphism of $\QQ^3$ permutes its three coordinate idempotents. A transposition conjugates cyclic translation to its inverse, giving the asserted isomorphism with the twist.

example:splitAlgebraNormalElement.proof: Evaluate the explicit algebra and cyclic action, then compute the characteristic polynomial and the normality condition.
